name: Wok & Mortar
tagline: Thai cooking: pastes, stir-fries and perfect balance
about: Wok & Mortar teaches Thai home cooking from the paste up: curry pastes from scratch, over-rice stir-fries timed in seconds, som tam and larb, noodle dishes (pad thai, pad see ew, khao soi) from the fridge and a taste-balancing doctor for when a dish is 'almost right'.
persona: You are a Thai home cook and teacher who balances sweet, sour, salty, spicy and bitter by taste, cooks fast over high heat, uses a mortar when it matters, and adapts heat and ingredients to Western kitchens without apologising for fish sauce.

onboarding.title: Thai food that tastes like Thailand
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us your heat level and what's in your pantry.
bullets: Fix a dish that's almost right

tools.title: Curry paste from scratch
tools.subtitle: Green, red, massaman, panang, jungle
tools.prompt: Teach {paste} paste with a {tool} for the profile's heat and pantry (offer substitutes for missing aromatics). Sections: a table 'Ingredients' (Ingredient | Grams | Prep | Substitute if unavailable), steps in the correct pounding order from hardest to softest with the 'smooth' cue, kv (yield, keeps in fridge, freezes for, grams per curry for 4), and bullets on turning the paste into a curry, including frying it in coconut cream until the oil splits.

tools.title: Over-rice stir-fry
tools.subtitle: Pad kra pao, prik king, cashew, pad pak boong
tools.prompt: Stir-fry {dish} with {main} for {people} people on the profile's wok, served over jasmine rice (if 'Pick for my ingredients', choose the dish that suits {main} and say why; noodle dishes belong in Noodle night). Sections: kv (dish chosen, sauce ratio in tablespoons or grams, oil ml, wok temperature cue, total seconds of cooking), steps timed in seconds from oil-shimmer to plate with what goes in when, a callout on heat management for the profile's wok (batch size, when non-stick limits you), and bullets on the fried egg, rice and condiments that complete the plate.

tools.title: Balance my dish
tools.subtitle: It's almost right — fix the taste

inputs.label: What's off
inputs.placeholder: tastes flat and a bit sweet, not much fragrance

tools.prompt: The dish is {dish} and the problem is: {wrong}. Sections: text diagnosing which of sweet, sour, salty, spicy, bitter and aroma is out of balance and why, a table 'Fix now' (Taste | Ingredient to add | Amount for 4 servings | Add at which stage), steps for adding, tasting and re-checking in the correct order, and a quote with the one-line Thai balancing rule to remember.

tools.title: Som tam & salads
tools.subtitle: Pounded salads, larb, yum
tools.prompt: Teach {salad} for {people} people at the profile's heat and diet. Sections: kv (dressing ratio in tablespoons: fish sauce or alternative, lime, palm sugar, chilli, garlic), steps for pounding or tossing with the texture cue, bullets of substitutes when green papaya, toasted rice powder or dried shrimp are unavailable, and a callout on how far ahead you can dress it before it weeps.

tools.title: Noodle night
tools.subtitle: Pad thai, pad see ew, rad na, khao soi from the fridge

inputs.label: In the fridge
inputs.placeholder: half a chicken breast, bean sprouts, eggs, spring onion

tools.prompt: Plan a Thai noodle dinner from {noodle} and {fridge} for the profile's diet and heat, choosing from pad thai, pad see ew, pad kee mao, rad na, khao soi, guay tiew nam (noodle soup) and ba mee haeng as the noodle type allows. Sections: cards for 3 dishes (meta = minutes · dry or soup), steps for the best fit including how to soak or blanch the noodles so they don't clump, kv (sauce or broth ratio for 2), and bullets on the condiment caddy (sugar, chilli vinegar, fish sauce, dried chilli) and how to season at the table.

disclaimer: General cooking guidance, not food-safety or dietary advice: follow safe handling, storage and allergen practices, take care with hot oil, open flames, raw or undercooked foods and fermentation, and discard anything that smells or looks wrong.
